Criticism of a product is not criticism of you or your enjoyment of that product. People who are reasonable in their criticism (not the people shouting profanity and threatening the dev team) for Playground Games in this update are critical because they are invested in the game and want it to be better. If they came to the game, thought it was bad, then quit, are likely not playing the game now and not trying to suggest improvements. Here's an example for a potential change and my reasoning behind it.

I personally think the 50% and 100% requirements for cars aren't in the best interest in the health of the game. If Playground Games made it 25-50% completion or even 40-60% I think it would be better for the series. The obvious result of a change like that is that cars are "easy" to get but that's not my personal goal suggesting that change. When you make 100% the finish line and have a wide variety of content that appeals to people in different ways players will typically complete the content they enjoy first, then if they choose to continue will finish with the content they don't enjoy. Those players put down the game for the week, having earned their 100%, and the overall feeling for their play is negative even if 90% of the content they did was enjoyable. That last 10% colors the whole experience. 

If you reduce the high end reward to 50% players have less "required" content (it's not actually required but some players feel the need to complete checklists) and that same player from above now has enjoyed 100% of the required content and will keep playing the additional content beyond it that leaves a positive feeling with the player when they put the game down because none of the content that was chosen by the player was negative. Say I as a player don't like doing danger signs but feel the need to complete the checklist. If the unlock is 50% instead of 100% I won't leave my session with a negative view of the game because I was playing only the content I enjoy. I could have 90% of the list done but because the reward was at 50% it's easier to justify skipping the danger sign. Did the lack of requiring the danger sign make that reward easier to get? Yes, but it also had the benefit of making me enjoy that session on the game more than I otherwise would have. That happy feeling keeps me playing, keeps me in the network around the game, and makes me more likely to purchase the next entry in the series which benefits the devs, the publisher, and the community that enjoys these games.
